prospect.training_background: Highly active by his own account: cycling, dumbbell work at home on his deck, swimming, basketball every Thursday for a couple of years, and a six to ten mile hike every Sunday. Before the gallbladder problem he was doing CrossFit alongside a weekly 36-hour fast, then stopped everything. Restarted dumbbell work about two months ago. Note an internal inconsistency in the transcript: he says early on "I don't have a gym membership" and later refers to "my CrossFit gym, next to my home, I go five times a week" at $149 a month with a nutrition coach.
prospect.medical: Gallbladder condition, still on prescription medication, which he associates directly with weight gain — 197 lb last year to 239 lb now, which he describes as roughly 50 pounds over nine months, gaining about five pounds a month. He raised the side-effect question with his doctor, who changed the prescription without effect and advised him simply to exercise more and reduce portions. Symptoms are controlled while medicated. Does not eat chicken on hormone grounds. No injuries or movement limitations were asked about. Sleep and energy were never asked about.

tiers.note: Off-menu. "Primal University" — named here for the first time in this batch — a monthly cancel-any-time subscription with the kettlebell exercise library, a three-month structured workout plan, a nutrition protocol and a weekly live training and Q&A with Trevor.

evidence: The rep disqualified him from the one-to-one programme on his own initiative: "from what I'm hearing, it's not something that you need to work one-on-one with Trevor. You're just dialing in what you're doing and sticking to the doctor's prescription, eating a little bit less."
The $6,000 offer was therefore never presented and no price for it was ever stated.
The $200/month alternative was explicitly declined on price and fit: "And then the program is not for me."

Counter-evidence: the rep offered to email details of the community product and the prospect said "That works. Thank you", so a small residual possibility remains — but he had already rejected it against a cheaper alternative he uses five times a week.
Recorded as lost rather than follow_up because the rep disqualified, which the vocabulary assigns to lost, and because the prospect gave an explicit no.
outcome.next_step: Rep to email information about the Primal University community subscription. No follow-up call booked.

notable.note: Two things worth a principal's attention. First, the good one: the rep disqualified honestly and quickly rather than pushing a $6,000 programme at someone whose problem is very likely a medication side effect, and he referred the issue back to the prospect's doctor. That is the right call and it is rare in this corpus. Second, the bad one: the prospect noticed the recording notice and asked directly whether the call was being published, and was told it was personal note-taking — "it's taking notes like for me I'm really really bad at taking notes." These recordings are stored, reviewed by his manager for coaching, and are the subject of this audit. Also note this is the second appearance in this batch of a $200/month subscription used as a downsell, here given a product name, Primal University, and that the rep twice questioned the prospect's doctor's reasoning out loud ("that's weird") while ultimately deferring to it.

quality.notes: The opening ninety seconds are a single undiarized block containing both speakers. Question ownership inverts repeatedly thereafter — "Well, noodles and rice, these are carbs" and "do you eat meat or not?" both sit under the wrong label, as does "It is what it is" in the closing exchange. Audio quality was poor and the rep asked the prospect to repeat himself three times; several phrases are clearly ASR-corrupted, notably "gold issue" and "gut-letter issue" for gallbladder, and "hundreds But 49 a month" where $149 is the most probable reading. The prospect's video never worked and the rep turned his own camera off.
